results.comment: 15:30 This part is kinda iffy for me.  Jaspreet is a millionaire with multiple income streams so I feel as though this advice is highly dependent on your income level: if you're not making a whole lot of money (like you're at the bottom 10-15% of the tax brackets), then sticking with your 401K and Roth IRA (even if you can't max them out) are your best options because time in the market beats timing the market, but as your tax bracket goes up, so do your options.  This part seems more like an aspirational goal rather than a start: it's like getting advice from a bodybuilder to start benching your bodyweight when you can barely push the bar off your chest.  Basically, a Roth IRA maxes out at $6,000 a year, right?  That's around $116 a week, give or take a few cents.  If you can't allocate that much money a week, then this part may not apply to you *right now*, but it should be a goal.

results.comment: 25:02 Real estate investors that do it right make money 5 ways.  Appreciation:  In single family homes, appreciation is speculation! Although it is one way we make money.  Leverage:  25% down-payment on a $100,000 house (example)  is $25,000, a10% return on $100,000 ($10,000) is a 40% return on your $25k. Not including principle paydown.  Principle paydown:  Every month a resident is living in your house (living in your house) they pay the rent(if done correct) , which in turn pays the mortgage, thus paying down the principle.  Depreciation:  The IRS allows you to use the depreciation of the improvements on your land over 27.5 years, making the money you earn through rent, tax deferred.  Cash flow:  If done right hopefully there is a little extra money every month through rent(along with other benefits)  that will be made while you own it that will be tax deferred through depreciation in the improvements.  And for a bonus, there's a 6th way (forced appreciation) but we won't get into that because it only deals with apartment.  Or, you could get or keep a job and continue trading YOUR time for money. And giving half of it to the government to do what they do with your money! I also forgot to mention equity capture. Buying a distressed property for 75%or less than the after repair value.
